- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast peak and introduce mild downward slope.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0 to 0.30) and price is trending up, model often overestimates momentum; reduce forecast slope slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.30) and price is near support, model tends to overreact; cap forecast at recent low or add slight resistance bias.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in high-sentiment periods; increase forecast variance or add 1-2% upward buffer for sentiment-driven spikes.
- Forecast horizon 30d often shows lag in response to sentiment shifts; delay peak forecast by 1-2 days if sentiment turns sharply positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.30 → -0.40 → +0.20), model tends to misread momentum; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment cycle lag.
